options.name: Formal 15-Day Statutory Demand Notice (Pre-Litigation)
options.summary: Send a formal legal notice via Registered Speed Post AD & Email giving 15 days to refund principal + 12% interest.
options.why_it_works: Over 75% of Indian consumer/tenancy disputes settle here when the party realizes you have exact statutory citations and court readiness.

options.name: National Consumer Helpline (NCH - 1915) / INGRAM Grievance
options.summary: Lodge an online complaint at consumerhelpline.gov.in or Toll-Free 1915. Government grievance officers summon the company's Nodal Officer.
options.why_it_works: Mandatory 30-day corporate response required under Ministry of Consumer Affairs rules.

options.name: Online Consumer Commission Petition (e-Daakhil / DCDRC)
options.summary: File a direct petition before the District Consumer Commission under Section 35 CPA 2019. Zero court fee up to ₹5 Lakh.
options.why_it_works: Consumers can argue their own case without hiring a private advocate. Forum awards refund + interest + harassment compensation.

Sincerely,

pillar_4_help_them_argue.objection: Our platform policy clearly states '7-day replacement only, strictly no refunds'. The 7-day window has expired, so the complaint is closed.
pillar_4_help_them_argue.intent: Invoking internal corporate policy to override statutory consumer rights.
pillar_4_help_them_argue.suggested_rebuttal: Internal company policy cannot override the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Under Section 2(10) and 2(11), supplying a defective product and failing to replace or repair it within a reasonable time constitutes gross deficiency in service. Denying a refund when replacement fails is an Unfair Trade Practice under Section 2(47), for which the Central Consumer Protection Authority has repeatedly penalized e-commerce platforms.

pillar_4_help_them_argue.objection: We are only an online intermediary platform under Section 79 of the IT Act. We don't make or sell the product. You must contact the third-party seller directly.
pillar_4_help_them_argue.intent: Claiming intermediary safe harbor to dodge responsibility.
pillar_4_help_them_argue.suggested_rebuttal: Under Rule 5 and Rule 6 of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, marketplace platforms that collect payments, manage logistics, and handle customer communication have direct statutory liability to maintain a Grievance Redressal mechanism. You cannot claim intermediary safe harbor when you facilitate payment and fulfillment.
